data.name: Groot OS — Real-Time Voice-Reactive AI Interface
data.description: End-to-end sub-1.5s speech-to-speech AI platform combining a Next.js/TypeScript live waveform UI with a FastAPI WebSocket audio pipeline powered by Groq Whisper v3-turbo, multi-LLM failover routing, and neural Edge TTS.

caseStudy.overview: Groot OS is a full-duplex conversational voice AI interface designed to eliminate the awkward multi-second pauses common in traditional request-response voice assistants. By streaming raw audio over WebSockets and chunking synthesized speech at the sentence boundary, it achieves sub-1.5s end-to-end conversational turnaround.
caseStudy.problem: Standard voice AI wrappers wait for a full transcription, a full LLM text completion, and a full TTS audio file before playing sound—resulting in 4–7 second delays and broken UX when a user tries to interrupt mid-sentence.
architecture: Frontend (Next.js + TypeScript): Captures microphone audio streams, renders real-time Canvas waveform telemetry, and manages Web Audio API playback queues with instant barge-in cancellation.
Transport Layer: Full-duplex WebSocket connection between the browser and FastAPI backend for zero-overhead audio chunk streaming.
Speech-to-Text: Routes incoming audio buffers to Groq Whisper v3-turbo for near-instant transcription.
Inference & Failover: Streams LLM tokens through a multi-provider failover router across Groq and OpenRouter to prevent rate-limit drops.
Streaming TTS: Buffers tokens only up to sentence boundaries and dispatches neural Edge TTS audio chunks back to the client while the LLM is still generating.
challenges: Eliminated audio stutter during playback by decoupling sentence-level TTS synthesis from WebSocket frame reception via an asynchronous playback queue.
Implemented client-side barge-in detection so speaking over the assistant immediately flushes queued audio buffers and aborts stale backend generation.
Added provider fallback logic so API rate limits or transient 429s automatically reroute without dropping the live voice session.

data.name: InLine — Real-Time Collaborative Code Editor
data.description: Full-duplex collaborative coding workspace (Google Docs for developers) built with a React/TypeScript Monaco Editor frontend and a distributed Node.js + Socket.io room synchronization backend delivering sub-20ms multi-cursor sync.

caseStudy.overview: InLine is a browser-based collaborative code editor engineered for pair programming, technical interviews, and live debugging. It pairs a responsive React + Monaco Editor frontend with a Node.js + Socket.io room synchronization server.
caseStudy.problem: Sharing code snippets over screen-share or chat breaks workflow during live interviews and debugging sessions. Teams need a zero-setup URL-based room where multiple developers can edit simultaneously with live cursor presence.
architecture: Editor Frontend (React + TypeScript): Integrates Monaco Editor / CodeMirror 6 with multi-language syntax highlighting, custom keybindings, and inline AI code assistance.
Real-Time Room Server (Node.js + Express + Socket.io): Manages isolated room lifecycles, participant presence tracking, and incremental delta broadcasts.
State Sync: Broadcasts document mutations and cursor coordinates across connected peers while preventing echo loops on the originating client.
challenges: Prevented infinite update loops between local editor `onChange` events and incoming Socket.io patches by tagging remote transactions before applying them to the editor model.
Handled abrupt disconnects and reconnects cleanly in room state so active participants never see stale ghost cursors.

data.name: CodeGraph — Interactive AST Visualizer
data.description: Developer productivity tool parsing GitHub repository ASTs and ES module imports into interactive dynamic dependency graphs with React Flow path tracing and Supabase PostgreSQL caching.

caseStudy.overview: CodeGraph helps engineers onboard onto unfamiliar GitHub repositories in seconds by statically parsing source files and ES module imports into an interactive, zoomable dependency graph.

highlights.label: Automated ES import & file tree extraction
PostgreSQL graph caching for instant reloads

caseStudy.problem: Understanding how modules connect in a new codebase requires manually jumping across dozens of files. Static directory trees show folder hierarchy, not actual import dependencies.
architecture: Repository Ingestion: Fetches repository file trees and source files via GitHub APIs and extracts ES module import/export edges.
Graph Visualization (React Flow): Renders modules as interactive nodes with animated dependency path tracing when hovering or selecting a file.
Persistence Layer (Supabase PostgreSQL): Caches parsed repository dependency graphs so repeat lookups render instantaneously without hitting GitHub API rate limits.
challenges: Resolved relative import paths (`../`, `./`, index barrels) accurately across nested TypeScript/JavaScript folder structures so edges map cleanly to actual repository files.
Cached serialized graph structures in Supabase to keep repeated explorations fast and resilient against GitHub unauthenticated rate limits.

data.name: Arclane — Autonomous SMB Workflow & Deployment Engine
data.description: 24/7 autonomous SMB workflow automation engine combining geographic business discovery, Next.js/Tailwind production site generation, programmatic Vercel REST deployments, and live Telegram Bot telemetry.

caseStudy.overview: Arclane is a 24/7 autonomous workflow engine built to discover local SMBs lacking a modern web presence, generate tailored responsive Next.js/Tailwind web previews, deploy them programmatically to Vercel, and report live pipeline telemetry over Telegram.
caseStudy.problem: Manual agency prospecting and custom preview site generation take hours per client and don't scale cleanly across fragmented local markets.
architecture: Discovery Worker (Node.js + Puppeteer): Executes bounded micro-locality grid hopping with coordinate jittering, rate limiting, and deduplication.
Preview Generator (Next.js + TailwindCSS): Hydrates responsive, mobile-first business landing pages dynamically from structured business metadata.
Deployment Pipeline: Pushes generated builds programmatically via Vercel REST APIs and tracks deployment status.
Control Plane: Exposes an interactive Telegram Bot HUD for pause/resume commands, locality status, and live conversion telemetry.
challenges: Added boundary exhaustion safeguards and persistent state checkpoints so long-running daemons recover gracefully after restarts without duplicating work.
Enforced strict environment separation and automated credential hygiene across both the engine repository and the nested web-dev-agency repository.

data.name: Wearable AI Reading & Multimodal Study Assistant
data.description: Hardware-software accessibility assistant pairing live camera OCR vision with Bluetooth foot-pedal navigation and Gemini Flash-Lite reasoning for real-time audio study narration.

caseStudy.overview: A hands-free wearable study and reading assistant built in Kotlin for Android. It combines live camera capture, Gemini Flash-Lite multimodal reasoning, Bluetooth foot-pedal input events, and Text-to-Speech narration so users can study printed material without touching a screen.
caseStudy.problem: Students with visual impairments or hands-busy study workflows struggle with touch-heavy mobile OCR apps that require constant screen tapping to capture, navigate, and replay audio.
architecture: Input Bus (Kotlin + Android Bluetooth HID): Maps physical foot-pedal key events to capture, next/previous section, and audio replay actions.
Vision & Reasoning: Captures frames from the Android camera and dispatches them to Gemini Flash-Lite for structured text extraction and concise explanations.
Audio Feedback: Streams responses through Android's native Text-to-Speech engine with low-latency playback controls.
challenges: Debounced hardware foot-pedal key events to prevent accidental double-captures during rapid page turning.
Optimized prompt framing for Gemini Flash-Lite so spoken TTS output stays concise and easy to follow without reading raw markdown punctuation aloud.

data.name: Robot — Multimodal AI Voice & Hardware Engine
data.description: Edge computing and multimodal AI robotics pipeline orchestrating localized sensory telemetry, speech synthesis, and dual-column LLM inference routers.

caseStudy.overview: Robot is a modular Python + FastAPI + Next.js voice and hardware orchestration engine built to unify real-time speech synthesis, tool execution, telemetry, and configurable dual-column custom LLM APIs.
caseStudy.problem: Robotics and edge assistant prototypes often tightly couple hardware control loops to a single cloud LLM vendor, making offline testing, provider switching, and audio telemetry brittle.
architecture: Core Engine (Python + FastAPI): Manages assistant state modes, active personalities, turn counts, and tool integrations.
Dual-Column LLM Router: Supports hot-swapping OpenAI-compatible providers (OpenRouter and custom inference endpoints) with unit-tested configuration persistence.
Voice Synthesis Edge Route (Next.js Edge Runtime): Streams synthesized SSML audio directly to the browser's Web Audio player.
challenges: Designed comprehensive pytest unit test suites with mocked engine fixtures to validate dual-provider configuration updates safely.
Parameterized client tokens and scrubbed historical OAuth caches from Git history to enforce strict open-source security hygiene.
